title: Implement declarative strategy triggers and deterministic due scheduler
description:
Build declarative strategy trigger types in mike_trade/scheduling/triggers.py and one engine-owned scheduler in mike_trade/scheduling/scheduler.py. Put the unit tests in tests/unit/test_scheduler_triggers.py.

Required behavior:
- Trigger declarations are frozen value objects. Strategies attach them to their BUY or SELL class through configuration. Supported kinds:
  - MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL (any new trade or bar for the symbol)
  - QUOTE_CHANGE (bid or ask actually changed)
  - CANDLE_CLOSED(timeframe), for 1m, 5m, 15m and any other configured timeframe the h.1 candle builders support
  - INTERVAL(seconds)
  - SESSION_OPEN
  - ENTRY_CUTOFF
  - SESSION_CLOSE
  - MANUAL
  Trigger declarations are validated at load time. A positive interval and a supported timeframe are required. An unknown kind raises a typed configuration error.
- The scheduler is a single asyncio-driven component owned by the engine. It is not a thread or task per symbol or per strategy. It keeps a registry of (symbol, strategy_id, side, trigger set) for roughly 1-10 watched symbols and every enabled strategy.
- Inputs are scheduling events:
  - market-data arrival or quote change carrying a snapshot version
  - candle-closed carrying (symbol, timeframe, bar end UTC)
  - session events from the h.3 calendar (open, entry cutoff, close)
  - control ticks from an injected clock
  - manual evaluation requests
- Output is an ordered list of immutable DueEvaluation records: symbol, strategy_id, side, trigger kind, snapshot_version, bar key, due_at UTC.
- A global control cadence is only an upper tick. A control tick must not make CANDLE_CLOSED or other closed-bar strategies re-evaluate when their (symbol, timeframe, last closed bar end, snapshot_version) watermark is unchanged. INTERVAL triggers fire at most once per elapsed interval, measured with the injected clock.
- Duplicate suppression: the same (strategy_id, side, symbol, trigger kind, bar key or snapshot_version) never yields more than one DueEvaluation.
- Ordering is deterministic for identical inputs. Sort by:
  1. due_at
  2. trigger priority: session events, then candle close, then quote/data, then interval, then manual
  3. symbol
  4. strategy_id
  5. side
- All times are timezone-aware UTC. Session boundaries come from the existing exchange calendar in America/New_York. Do not hardcode wall-clock hours.
- Paused strategies, disabled strategies and unwatched symbols produce no DueEvaluation. MANUAL still produces one only when explicitly requested for an enabled strategy and watched symbol.
- The scheduler never evaluates strategies, calls brokers, opens data connections, or submits orders. It only decides what is due.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/scheduling/calendar.py (h.3) for session open, entry cutoff and close
- mike_trade/market_data/candles.py (h.1) for timeframe and closed-bar types
- mike_trade/market_data/context.py (h.4) for snapshot version semantics
- mike_trade/strategies/base.py, mike_trade/strategies/registry.py and mike_trade/domain/strategy_types.py (if present) for strategy identity and side types
- any existing clock port under mike_trade/ports/ or mike_trade/domain/ (if present)
acceptance_criteria: A test constructs each supported trigger kind (MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL, QUOTE_CHANGE, CANDLE_CLOSED for 1m/5m/15m, INTERVAL, SESSION_OPEN, ENTRY_CUTOFF, SESSION_CLOSE, MANUAL) and confirms it is frozen. Negative tests confirm that a non-positive interval, an unsupported timeframe and an unknown kind each raise a typed configuration error.

A test confirms that a CANDLE_CLOSED(1m) strategy yields exactly one DueEvaluation per newly closed bar. Repeated control ticks with an unchanged closed-bar watermark yield zero additional evaluations.
A test confirms that an INTERVAL(30s) trigger fires at most once per elapsed 30 seconds under an injected fake clock, regardless of how many control ticks occur.
A test confirms that QUOTE_CHANGE fires only when bid or ask actually changes. An identical repeated quote yields nothing.
A test confirms that SESSION_OPEN, ENTRY_CUTOFF and SESSION_CLOSE fire once per session at the times the injected calendar reports, including an early-close session.

A test feeds the same event sequence twice, including simultaneous events across several symbols and strategies, and confirms identical DueEvaluation output order both times, matching the documented sort key.
Tests confirm that disabled or paused strategies and unwatched symbols produce no DueEvaluation, and that MANUAL produces one only on explicit request.

A test or code-level assertion confirms the scheduler does not create a thread or asyncio task per symbol or per strategy. Registering 10 symbols with several strategies leaves the live task/thread count unchanged.
The scheduler modules import no broker or provider adapter, and tests run only with injected fakes and a fake clock.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
modify calendar.py, candles.py, context.py or strategy base/registry modules; adapt via their public APIs only
evaluate strategies, call brokers, open data connections or submit orders from the scheduler
create a thread, process or asyncio task per symbol or per strategy
use naive datetimes or hardcode session wall-clock hours
run broad test suites or backtests
